Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on any consumer hardware. Strata inference engine, but without the bloatware. Designed with containerized environments in mind. OpenAI/Anthropic API on localhost, optional image input.
On-device inference engine for non-LLM models: embeddings, SPLADE, multimodal. CPU/Metal/CUDA, daemon or in-process.

A bare-metal heterogeneous LLM inference engine engineered in C to shatter consumer hardware limits. Noel streams massive out-of-core models directly from NVMe SSDs into hybrid CPU (AVX-VNNI/AVX2) and GPU pipelines with dynamic MoE activation & priority tiering. Maximize every byte of VRAM, RAM, and SSD.
LLM local inference engine optimized for MOE-Models (like Kimi3.1) with SSD streaming
97 tested hypotheses on making huge MoE LLMs fast on consumer GPUs (4x RTX 3090 + experts in RAM): what worked, what failed and why. A playbook for people and a ready skill for coding agents.
Browser-local decision model inference with TVM WebGPU and ONNX Runtime Web
GPT-2 inference from scratch in Rust: faster than llama.cpp, ONNX Runtime and CTranslate2 on 4 CPU cores, and runs in the browser on WebGPU
Browser-native AI inference engine with WebGPU and WebAssembly acceleration. Run LLMs locally without servers, preserving privacy.
A from-scratch WebGPU inference engine: Whisper in the browser, 4.5-6.5x faster than Transformers.js
Run GLM-5.3-Flash (102 GB MoE) on one consumer GPU: a Rust + CUDA inference engine that streams experts from NVMe, with an OpenAI-compatible server
Purpose-built Rust inference engines for Snapdragon X CPUs: a static-plan MoE engine with MTP verify lanes, SSD expert streaming for a 125B MoE in 32 GB, and an int8 image engine.

A custom fork for frontier-scale mixture-of-experts inference on an RTX 3060 with 12 GB VRAM, 16 GB system RAM and local NVMe.**  Betelgeuse keeps dense computation on the GPU and brings routed experts into a bounded VRAM pool only when needed.

llama.cpp fork for significantly improved performance on Ampere generation Nvidia cards (especially RTX 3090 / 3090 Ti): example: 110+ tok/s over a 100K-token generation at temperature 1 for qwen3.8, supporting full 262K ctx. Supports low memory (12gb) configs for 200k+ ctx. 120+ TPS, 3300+ prefill for QFN 3.8.
A modular and open-ended toolkit for WebGPU, with advanced type inference and the ability to write shaders in TypeScript

Open-source local AI SDK - run AI on-device with no cloud, no API keys. Supports GGUF, RAG, image, music, and video generation, speech-to-text, P2P inference, and more. Cross-platform: Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS.
Turn your Mac into a local LLM server: MLX on Metal, OpenAI + Anthropic API + MCP, pure Swift. Point Claude Code at it.
Stable, high-throughput inference server for multi-GPU NVIDIA V100 (SM70): Qwen3.8 Flash-Next with AWQ / NVFP4, multimodal input, CPU/disk KV offload, and MTP or DFlash2 speculative decoding.
Pulsar (formerly fastkernel): the fastest inference engine for Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Inkling 2 Mini on Apple Silicon
LLM Inference Engine for Metal, CUDA and Vulkan.

One binary to rule them all: model-agnostic local LLM inference for AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI MAX+ 395) on Linux. Radeon 8060S iGPU (gfx1151) via HRX + our HIP kernels, XDNA 2 NPU via our NPU runtime, inside Lemonade Server with an OpenAI-compatible API. Qwen3.8, ZAYA1, BitNet b1.58, any GGUF. Apache-2.0.
LLM inference server with continuous batching & SSD caching for Apple Silicon — managed from the macOS menu bar
Run models larger than your RAM or VRAM by streaming MoE experts from SSD. Built on llama.cpp.

Local inference you can prove. A single-binary GGUF engine in C: serves, scores, and trains LoRA through the quantized weights it deploys, byte-reproducibly. Tool calls survive the token limit; every run replays as a signed receipt. CPU/CUDA/Metal, OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible.
Run Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B) on an RTX 3060 12 GB with 30 GB of RAM, streaming experts from the SSD. 50-70 tok/s, 262K context. A fork of Strata.
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on any consumer hardware: one-click install for Windows / Linux. Strata inference engine, OpenAI/Anthropic API on localhost, optional image input.

Run MoE models bigger than your RAM. Frontier-size MoE on a phone, laptop, edge. Lossless, on stock llama.cpp. An adaptive streaming optimizer. Any hardware, any OS, any model, any quantization, behind a local OpenAI-compatible server.

Fully local AI coding agent for a regular consumer gaming PC: own inference engine with an MoE expert cache, a coding agent with undo for destructive actions, and a split that keeps your desktop smooth while the model works.
High-performance Ultralytics YOLO inference in Rust with ONNX Runtime, GPU backends, CLI, and WebGPU/WASM.

Pure-Rust local inference for language, vision, image, speech and embedding models from Hugging Face (safetensors, GGUF, MLX). SIMD CPU kernels everywhere, Metal, CUDA and Vulkan GPUs, a WebAssembly + WebGPU browser build, and an OpenAI-compatible server.
An anomaly detection library comprising state-of-the-art algorithms and features such as experiment management, hyper-parameter optimization, and edge inference.
Fast KV-cache quantization for Apple Silicon (MLX) — 43 research-adapted compression methods with Metal kernels
A hierarchical inference engine for frontier MoE models: hot experts on the GPU (CUDA, Vulkan), warm ones in RAM, cold ones streamed from NVMe. Written in C, runs on the hardware you already own.
The local AI app built for the Mac. Run LLMs like Qwen, Gemma and GPT-OSS on Apple Silicon, including models far bigger than your Mac's memory, by streaming MoE experts from the SSD.
A PyTorch-native inference engine with cache, parallelism, quantization and cpu offload for DiTs.

Run 50-280 GB MoE LLMs (DeepSeek V4/V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Ornith) on one consumer GPU: experts spread over VRAM, RAM and NVMe SSD. Browser chat + OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. CUDA, ROCm, DGX Spark.
A low-level llama.cpp runtime for browser applications. This repository builds WebAssembly and Emscripten JavaScript, then publishes the runtime package to a separate Git branch.

Run Mixture-of-Experts LLMs (Qwen3, gpt-oss, GLM, DeepSeek) bigger than your RAM with llama.cpp: hot experts cached in RAM, the rest streamed from SSD. Windows (Vulkan/AMD, NVIDIA) and Linux, long context, coding agents.
Client-side WebGPU/WASM ONNX inference and Matryoshka embedding engine
Zero-dependency JS+WGSL runtime for AI workloads

Rapid-MLX is an open-source (Apache 2.0) OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX, focused on reliable tool calling for coding agents. Up to 4× faster than Apple's MLX (mlx-lm) on the same weights.
Run and fine-tune MoE models bigger than your Mac's RAM. PagedMoE streams experts from SSD on demand with MLX on Apple Silicon.
An optimized quantization and inference library for running LLMs locally on modern consumer-class GPUs
Run local AI models anywhere

Local AI platform: WebGPU/WGSL browser inference engine + HuggingFace Transformers + Ollama. TurboQuant KV cache compression, GPTQ INT4 fused dequant, mixed-precision BF16/INT4 for hybrid SSM+attention models. 9B parameters in a browser, 8GB VRAM.
Turn your Android phone into an OpenAI-compatible LLM inference server - Fully local, private and Open Source
Fast and lightweight SSD-streaming engine for MoE models on Apple Silicon with MLX
Run and serve local LLMs everywhere .NET runs - desktop and the browser - on the SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML inference engine (GGUF models, KV-cache decode, WebGPU dispatch-plan capture/replay).
Kyojin: open-source engine that runs 100 GB-class open models (GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek V4.1) on one desktop machine. AMD Strix Halo, NVIDIA RTX and Apple Mac. OpenAI API, built on ExLlamaV3.

The local inference server for coding agents. Pure Rust, one binary, Apple Silicon + NVIDIA. Anthropic + OpenAI APIs; the KV cache survives across turns, so turn 20 starts as fast as turn 2. OPD training on the same runtime.
Glyd is a fast inference engine for open LLMs with lossless GPU compression, from a laptop GPU to multi-GPU servers. One program, no Python.
Cross-platform audio processing SDK for React Native — streaming, recording, analysis, visualization, and on-device inference
Remove image backgrounds entirely in the browser with ONNX Runtime Web (WASM + WebGPU). No upload, no server, no API key. Includes a benchmark probe comparing WASM and WebGPU inference times.

An AI agent you build, not just prompt. Local-first Android agent with on-device inference (LiteRT-LM), pipelines you assemble yourself, MCP tool calling, and your confirmation before any risky action.
Unofficial ONNX Runtime Web build with faster WebGPU kernels for quantized LLMs (for Quick Inference)
High-performance In-browser LLM Inference Engine

Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B local inference engine for Vulkan and Metal
A from-scratch deep learning framework in pure Rust: autograd, parallel GEMM, WebGPU, and inference for BERT, ViT, Whisper and LLMs from Hugging Face checkpoints.
⚡ Zero-Stall MoE Inference via Lookahead Prediction & Async DMA Prefetching. Optimized for SSD I/O with Hybrid MLA+Sliding Window Attention.
edge-dit.cpp — a native C/C++ inference engine for Diffusion Transformers (DiT), designed for local and resource-constrained devices with automatic VRAM-aware precision, placement, and offloading.
Go AI engine — layers, quants/k-quants, and backends (CPU SIMD, WebGPU, CUDA, Metal, MLX, Vulkan, ROCm, QNN)
Experimental Python/MLX inference runtime for Apple Silicon, with SSD-streamed MoE experts, bounded caching and Metal kernels. Alpha.

Run a 105 GB AI model on a Mac that can't hold it. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 4-bit, streamed from SSD on 16–64 GB Apple Silicon Macs. Fully native Swift, MLX and Metal. Offline, no Python. CLI, Swift library, and Ollama/OpenAI/Anthropic APIs. Works with Claude Code and Codex.
Camelid: a Rust-native local inference backend with evidence-gated model compatibility.

FEDML - The unified and scalable ML library for large-scale distributed training, model serving, and federated learning. FEDML Launch, a cross-cloud scheduler, further enables running any AI jobs on any GPU cloud or on-premise cluster. Built on this library, TensorOpera AI (https://TensorOpera.ai) is your generative AI platform at scale.
⚡ Pure-Rust WebGPU inference engine — OpenAI-API compatible, GGUF native, runs on any GPU. No Python. No llama.cpp. Single binary.
Pure-Rust WebGPU inference engine for GGUF models. No C++, no Python, no llama.cpp. Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Apple Silicon.
A streaming Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference engine written in pure C, that runs models larger than your RAM on ordinary consumer hardware - MiniMax-M2 (230B) - GPT-OSS (20B and 120B) and Qwen3-MoE

AI inference, packed simply. A blazing-fast, zero-dependency WebGPU runtime to run GGUF models directly in the browser. Features a symmetric API for seamless local execution and cloud provider routing. Built with Rust & C++.
Hybrid Lean 4 + GPU 1.58-bit neural network quantizer combining machine-checked L1 median optimality proofs (l1-projection-complexity-lean4 v4.0.0) with CUDA/PyTorch LinearSelector kernels.
Does LLM quantization make voice-agent tool-calling more fragile to ASR noise? No — 2-bit ≈ 5-bit on BFCL under ASR noise, CPU/GGUF. Code, data & paper.
Can LLM agents write correct and fast quantized GPU kernels? A 40-operator benchmark with bit-exact and format-derived oracles, mutation-tested.
Kevin AI - C99 CPU inference engine for small language models on a small machine (Qwen3.5-4B, Gemma 4 E4B)

CuTileForge v3.0.0: Native tile-fusion compiler & universal quantization engine on NVIDIA CuTile. Zero-ATen CUDA-graph decode at 172 tok/s, 2,377 tok/s batch serving, 13 model families, 70B hybrid on a single 32 GB GPU (sm_89 ↔ sm_120).
Model-specific megakernel inference engines for LLM decoding, written by coding agents. OpenAI-compatible server, evaluation suite, and the kit to build your own.
A single-binary local LLM inference server in Rust + C. Supports Safetensors (F32/F16/BF16)  CPU/Vulkan. OpenAI-compatible gateway
Delta Inference Engine: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one NVIDIA GPU, natively on Windows (OpenAI-compatible server)

Rust bindings for ncnn inference with resource-safe ownership, reusable output buffers and an optional Vulkan backend.
A dependency-free C inference engine for Liquid AI's LFM2 / LFM2.5 models. Terminal chat, an OpenAI-compatible server, a web agent and a terminal agent, all in one executable.
Web UI to pool your home machines into one llama.cpp cluster: multi-machine RPC GPU pooling + on-demand multi-model serving via llama-swap
Live, multi-camera object tracking with SAM3, SAM 2 and EdgeTAM, on one GPU or many. One model per GPU serves every camera: faster than the original code, about 4x less GPU memory, the same accuracy.

Build, train, optimize, and run computer vision models locally, from raw images to live inference. Open source, optimized for Intel® XPU (CUDA also supported).

Self-hosted LLM inference mesh in .NET. One Ollama-compatible API in front, a pool of GPU worker nodes behind it — run the hub where you have no GPU, run nodes where you do. Pluggable backends (Ollama first).
A GPU cluster manager for high-performance AI model serving (vLLM, SGLang) and on-demand SSH-accessible GPU instances.

A dashboard for a home cluster of NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark / ASUS GX10) inference servers: GPU and system health, plus live per-model metrics from llama.cpp, vLLM, TensorFold, and SGLang.

Nano Quant Engine (NanoQuat-O2) — a pure-C, sub-bit weight-packing and streaming inference engine. Packs 3.83B weights into 75 MB (0.157 bits per weight, codebook included) and streams them back at up to 231M weights/sec with a 4.5 MB resident footprint. Deterministic and hash-verified; builds with a C compiler and nothing else.
